score_rationale: SGDD is an algorithm; its core (Algorithm 1 + Eq 10/11/12/13 + Sec C.3 schedule) is mechanically verified on CPU with no weights (7/7 tests): potential divergence, the beta~==beta_t prior-step identity, MH detailed-balance invariance, and end-to-end convergence to the EXACT synthetic posterior (Hellinger 0.40->0.19 with budget, reaching the paper's D=2 target 0.149, matching Theorem 1's O(1/K)). Held below 1.0 for two reasons stated openly: (a) the paper's competitive RANKING vs DPS/SMC/SVDD-PM is NOT reproduced because our minimal synthetic task is too easy to trigger the baselines' documented prior-collapse (root cause: undisclosed multivariate forward model f), and (b) real-data DNA/MNIST/music metrics are gated on the SEDD-90M priors. Not lowered further because the algorithm itself is fully correct and its accuracy claim is measured against ground truth, not asserted.

components_verified: Potential D(x,z;eta) (Eq 10): diverges as eta->0 for Hamming>0, =0 when x=z
Prior-step identity (Eq 11 == Eq 12): beta~(eta) == beta_t(sigma=eta) EXACTLY
Metropolis-Hastings likelihood step (Eq 13): leaves target exp(-f-D) invariant (detailed balance, recovers target Hellinger<0.15)
Geometric annealing schedule (Sec C.3): eta_k = eta_min^{k/K} eta_max^{1-k/K}, endpoints + strict decrease
End-to-end synthetic D=2: converges to the exact true posterior; beats prior-collapse; Hellinger decreases with budget per Theorem 1
algorithm_verification.note: The paper's core contribution — the split-Gibbs discrete posterior sampler — is mechanically verified without any trained weights: the Eq 11/12 identity is exact, MH invariance holds, and SGDD provably approaches the analytic posterior with O(1/K) convergence.
